badBuilds.notes: NH36 is vendor-confirmed day-date ('three-hand day-date' per Lucius's guide; Namoki separately sells a dedicated 'NH36 Intermediate Wheel for Day Corrector' spare part, confirming day hardware is NH36-specific). This dial is explicitly 'Sterile - No Date' -- no day or date aperture at all. Unlike good-020 (where a sterile dial over NH36 is a deliberate, informed cosmetic choice), this fixture models the beginner mistake of not realizing NH36 costs more specifically for a day-date function the dial can't display -- should block or at minimum hard-warn, not silently pass as equivalent to an NH35 build.

badBuilds.notes: NH34 is a GMT movement (vendor-confirmed: 'GMT, available since 2022... the only NH movement for travel-watch builds'), which needs a dial with a GMT sub-scale/marker and GMT-capable hands (a 4th, 24-hour hand) to be meaningful. This dial/hands pair has no GMT features -- physically the movement may still fit the case (same nh3x footprint), but the GMT function is wasted and the standard 3-hand hands will not mount the 4th GMT hand pinion NH34 has, which is a real fitment failure, not just a styling gap. All 5 parts audited.

parts.dial: Lucius Atelier Vintage Enamel Biege Dial (Date)
parts.bezelInsert: Namoki SKX007/SRPD Steel Bezel Insert: Nautical Steel

badBuilds.notes: This exact movement SKU is titled 'Date @ 6H' -- a real, non-default date-wheel position, distinct from the two conventions Lucius's own guide documents ('3 o'clock suits classic divers. 4:30 is a Seiko hallmark'). The dial's date cutout position was not independently confirmed in this session (audit row is medium confidence, family-inferred). Modeling the case where a movement's date-wheel position and a dial's date-cutout position are assumed to match without checking -- a real, documented failure mode (see also Watch & Style's real 'W1441 5 o'clock Window Date Wheel Disc' SKU, proving position varies).

badBuilds.notes: THE key false-positive-trap fixture. This case's own body_html states directly: 'standard SKX bezels, inserts, and crystals will not fit, and ours will not fit a stock SKX.' The bezel insert used here is a standard fits-skx013 SKU (not one of Lucius's own Ultra Thin-scoped accessories), so despite every part individually being a real, high-confidence, vendor-tagged 'skx013' part, the case is a proprietary redesign that rejects them. This is the single most important bad-build fixture in the set -- if Phase 2's rules pass this as compatible, the zero-false-positive guarantee has already failed.

badBuilds.notes: Modeled on a real, narrated bad build from WatchUSeek user 'begud' (quoted by 'adamjaffeback' in post #15,161 on the 'Post your mods here' megathread): an SKX013-class build with a DLW dial/hands pairing and a Lucius Atelier bezel/insert/chapter-ring pairing that, per the poster's own account, resulted in the bezel not turning, the second hand touching the crystal when the case back was fully screwed down, and a misaligned day disc. The exact SKUs in that 2020 post are not identifiable/live today, so this fixture substitutes current, audited SKUs from the same vendors in the same rough roles (DLW dial+hands, Lucius bezel insert) rather than quoting the original SKUs verbatim. Compounded here with a day-date NH36 on a no-date dial (see bad-001) as the primary, cleanly-testable error; the original post's issues were more about a specific low-quality third-party case's tolerances than a family mismatch.
